name: sql-authoring
description: Rules for writing correct, readable, cheap SQL: CTE structure, join and NULL pitfalls, safe defaults (row limits, time filters, PII). Load before writing any non-trivial query (joins, aggregation, window functions, dedupe).
body:
# SQL authoring

## Before writing
- Parse the request into: output columns, grain (one row per what), filters, aggregations, joins, ordering, row limit.
- Take every table/column name from the DB metadata block. If a needed column is missing, say so; never invent one.
- Ask OpenMetadata (if available) for meaning when a column name is ambiguous (status codes, amount units, soft-delete flags).

## Structure
- One CTE per logical step, descriptive names; no deeply nested subqueries.
- Name columns explicitly; no SELECT * outside throwaway exploration. Qualify every column with a table alias in joins.
- Comment the why of non-obvious filters, not the what.

## Correctness traps
- Grain first: joining a 1-to-many table then SUM()ming a parent column multiplies it. Aggregate the child first (CTE), then join, or use the parent key with COUNT(DISTINCT).
- INNER vs LEFT JOIN: a filter on the right table in WHERE turns a LEFT JOIN into an INNER JOIN; put it in ON.
- NULL: = NULL never matches; NOT IN (subquery with NULL) returns nothing, prefer NOT EXISTS; COUNT(col) skips NULLs, COUNT(*) does not; SUM over zero rows is NULL.
- Division: guard the denominator (NULLIF(x, 0)); integer / integer truncates in PostgreSQL and Trino (Oracle does not): cast to a decimal first.
- Average of averages is wrong: recompute from sums and counts.
- Percentages: say what the denominator is. Partial periods (this month so far) must not be compared with full ones.
- Dedupe with ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY key ORDER BY updated_at DESC) = 1, state which row wins and why.
- Time zones: say which one boundaries use; truncate to day in the reporting zone, not blindly in UTC.
- Prefer EXISTS over IN for correlated membership tests; avoid correlated subqueries in SELECT lists on large tables.

## Cheap by default
- Exploration queries get a row limit (Oracle FETCH FIRST n ROWS ONLY; PostgreSQL/Trino LIMIT n). Aggregations over big tables get a time or partition filter.
- Filter early, on indexed/partition columns, with plain comparisons (see query-performance for sargability).
- Select only needed columns. Pre-aggregate in SQL; never return more than a few thousand rows for a chart.

## Sensitive data
- If metadata tags/names mark PII (phone, email, card, CCCD/ID number, address, account number), do not SELECT it raw unless the user asked; mask or aggregate, and say so.
- Never put credentials or real customer values into proposed SQL.

## Write statements
INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL need an explicit warning that the statement modifies data and needs separate approval. UPDATE/DELETE must carry a WHERE; propose the matching SELECT COUNT(*) first.

name: sql-review
description: Checklist to review, validate or double-check SQL (yours or pasted by the user) without running it: grain, join fan-out, aggregation, NULL, cost and safety, plus verification queries and a confidence rating. Load when asked to review/check/validate/verify a query or before finalizing a multi-table query.
body:
# SQL review (static; you cannot execute)

Work through the groups in order. Mark each finding Severity High / Medium / Low.

## 1. Grounding
- Every table and column exists in the DB metadata block (case/quoting per dialect). Unknown names are High.
- Types compatible in joins and comparisons (number vs string, date vs varchar). Implicit casts on indexed columns kill index use.

## 2. Grain and joins
- State the grain of each CTE/table. Use PK/FK info from metadata: is each join key unique on the side that should be unique?
- 1-to-many join feeding SUM/COUNT of a parent column = fan-out (High). Safer: pre-aggregate the many side.
- LEFT JOIN with a right-table predicate in WHERE (silently INNER). Missing join condition = cartesian product.
- Many-to-many joins without a bridge/dedupe.

## 3. Aggregation and metrics
- Every non-aggregated SELECT column is in GROUP BY (Oracle ORA-00979 / PostgreSQL 42803).
- Denominator can be zero or NULL; ratios of ratios; average of averages; percentages summing to ~100 when they should.
- Partial period compared with a full one; YoY/MoM base period correct; time zone consistent.
- DISTINCT used as a band-aid for a join problem (hides fan-out).

## 4. Filters and NULLs
- NOT IN with nullable subquery; = NULL; OR conditions that defeat partition pruning; status/soft-delete flags (deleted_at, is_active, test accounts) handled as the business definition says (ask OpenMetadata or the user).

## 5. Cost and safety
- No time/partition filter on a large table; function on a filtered column (see query-performance); SELECT *; unbounded result; ORDER BY without LIMIT on a huge set.
- Write statements: WHERE present, matching SELECT COUNT(*) proposed, transaction advice.
- PII columns returned raw.

## 6. Dialect
- Syntax matches the connection dialect (LIMIT vs FETCH FIRST, || NULL handling, date functions, ILIKE not in Oracle/Trino).

## Output format
```
## Validation report
Overall: <Ready to run | Run with noted caveats | Needs revision>
### Issues (Severity: High|Medium|Low) — each with line/CTE and the fix
### Verification queries (user runs these; paste results back)
### Assumptions / caveats
```

## Verification queries to propose (adapt names and dialect)
- Fan-out check: COUNT(*) of the base table vs COUNT(*) after each join; or COUNT(*) - COUNT(DISTINCT key) on the join key.
- Duplicate key check: SELECT key, COUNT(*) FROM t GROUP BY key HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 (limit 20).
- Reconciliation: SUM of the metric from the source table vs from the final query for the same filter.
- Null rate of the join/filter columns.

## When the user pastes results back
Red flags: change >50% period over period with no known cause; exact round numbers; rates exactly 0% or 100%; identical values across segments or periods (a dimension is ignored); results that confirm the hypothesis too perfectly. Say what you would check next.

name: query-performance
description: Diagnose and fix slow queries: sargable predicates, index design (composite order, FK indexes, partial/covering), keyset pagination, N+1, and how to read EXPLAIN in PostgreSQL, Oracle and Trino. Load for slow query, timeout, memory limit, EXPLAIN, index or pagination questions.
body:
# Query performance

## Principles
- Measure, do not guess: ask for the plan, then change one thing.
- Reduce rows early (filters on partition/indexed columns), then join, then aggregate, then sort.

## Sargable predicates (all dialects)
Do not wrap the filtered column in a function or cast; move the work to the constant side.
```
-- bad: index/partition on created_at unusable
WHERE TRUNC(created_at) = DATE '2025-01-15'        -- Oracle
WHERE date(created_at) = '2025-01-15'              -- PostgreSQL / Trino
WHERE to_char(created_at,'YYYY-MM') = '2025-01'
-- good: half-open range on the raw column
WHERE created_at >= DATE '2025-01-15' AND created_at < DATE '2025-01-16'
```
Also: leading-wildcard LIKE '%x', implicit type conversion (string column vs number), OR across different columns, and col + 1 = x defeat indexes. Trino/Hive-style tables: filter partition columns (ds, dt, year/month/day) with plain comparisons.

## Indexes (PostgreSQL / Oracle)
- Index the columns in WHERE and JOIN. Foreign keys are NOT auto-indexed in PostgreSQL or Oracle: an unindexed FK makes joins and parent deletes scan the child.
- Composite index: equality columns first, then range column; leftmost-prefix rule: (status, created_at) does not serve a filter on created_at alone.
- PostgreSQL partial index (WHERE deleted_at IS NULL) when queries repeat the predicate; INCLUDE columns for index-only scans. Oracle: function-based index only when the function cannot be removed from the predicate.
- Low-cardinality column alone is a poor B-tree key; BRIN (PostgreSQL) for huge append-only time data; GIN for jsonb/array/full-text.

## Pagination
OFFSET n reads and discards n rows. Use keyset: WHERE (created_at, id) > (:last_created_at, :last_id) ORDER BY created_at, id LIMIT 50 (Oracle: FETCH FIRST 50 ROWS ONLY with an equivalent OR-expanded predicate).

## Other patterns
- N+1: replace per-row lookups with a join or key = ANY(array)/IN list.
- COUNT(DISTINCT) on huge data: approx_distinct (Trino), APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT (Oracle 12c+), HyperLogLog extension in PostgreSQL, if exact is not required.
- Bulk write: multi-row INSERT / INSERT ... SELECT, MERGE or ON CONFLICT for upsert.
- UNION ALL instead of UNION when duplicates are impossible or acceptable.

## Reading the plan
### PostgreSQL
```
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) SELECT ...
```
ANALYZE EXECUTES the statement: only propose it for SELECT, or for DML inside BEGIN ... ROLLBACK. Look for: Seq Scan on a big table; "Rows Removed by Filter" huge; estimated rows vs actual rows far apart (run ANALYZE table); Nested Loop with high loops; Sort Method: external merge (work_mem); Buffers read >> hit.
### Oracle
Two separate statements (run one by one):
```
EXPLAIN PLAN FOR SELECT ...
SELECT * FROM TABLE(DBMS_XPLAN.DISPLAY)
```
Look for: TABLE ACCESS FULL on big tables, Cartesian join, E-Rows vs A-Rows mismatch (stale stats: DBMS_STATS.GATHER_TABLE_STATS, DBA task), index range scan vs fast full scan, high Cost step.
### Trino
```
EXPLAIN SELECT ...
EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT ...
SHOW STATS FOR schema.table
```
(EXPLAIN ANALYZE runs the query.) Look for: full table scan with no pushed-down predicate (TupleDomain / partition filter missing), large REPARTITION/exchange, join order with the big table on the build (right) side. Remedies: filter partitions, project fewer columns, approx_* functions, SET SESSION join_distribution_type = 'BROADCAST' when the right side is small. Memory errors: narrow the range, pre-aggregate, avoid ORDER BY on huge sets, use approx_*.

name: data-profiling
description: How to explore and profile an unfamiliar table: classify columns, decide what OpenMetadata already answers, generate ONE consolidated profiling query, interpret null/cardinality/distribution findings. Load for "explore", "what is in this table", data-quality or profiling requests.
body:
# Data profiling (propose queries; the user runs them)

## Step 1 - take what metadata already knows (no SQL needed)
From the DB metadata block and OpenMetadata: columns, types, keys, descriptions, owner, tags (PII / tier), glossary terms, lineage (upstream sources, downstream consumers), existing profiler stats. Say which of these you could not find.

## Step 2 - classify columns
Identifier, Dimension (low-cardinality category), Metric (numeric measure), Temporal, Text, Boolean/flag, Structural (json/array).

## Step 3 - ONE profiling query for what metadata lacks
Single statement with CTEs / UNION ALL, row-limited or sampled if the table is big (time filter first). Cover per column type:
- all: total rows, null count and rate, distinct count (approx if huge).
- key candidates: COUNT(*) vs COUNT(DISTINCT key) to test uniqueness.
- numeric: min, max, avg, median/percentiles (p50, p95, p99), zero and negative counts.
- string: min/max length, empty strings, top 10 values with counts.
- date: min, max, rows in the future, gaps per day/month.
- boolean: true rate.
Keep it to at most ~15 columns per query; split otherwise.

## Step 4 - interpret pasted results
- Nulls: >5% warn, >20% alert. Completeness bands: >99% complete, 95-99% mostly, 80-95% incomplete, <80% sparse.
- Cardinality ratio near 1 = identifier; 3-50 distinct = good dimension.
- Placeholders as data: 0, -1, 999999, 'N/A', 'TBD', 'test'; one value dominating (default); stale updated_at; impossible values; inconsistent spellings (US / USA / United States); numbers stored as strings; status completed but completed_at NULL.
- Distribution words to use: skewed, bimodal, long tail, seasonal, change point, day-of-week effect.

## Output format
```
## Data profile: <table>
### Overview (grain, keys, size if known, freshness, owner, tags)
### Columns (name, type, class, what is known, what the profiling query will tell)
### Profiling query (one block)
### Data-quality risks (severity)
### Suggested next analyses (3-5, concrete: "trend of <metric> by <time col> split by <dimension>")
```

name: chart-selection
description: Pick the right chart (bar, line, pie, kpi) from the shape of the result and write a valid chart block plus the aggregating SQL for it. Load when the user asks for a chart, report, KPI, trend or dashboard panel.
body:
# Chart selection

The UI renders one chart per proposed SQL, from a fenced chart block with a single JSON object:
```
{"kind":"bar|line|pie|kpi","x":"<result column>","y":["<numeric result column>"],"agg":"sum|avg|count|none","title":"<insight>"}
```
x and y must be column names/aliases of the SQL you proposed. The user applies it after running the query.

## Choose from the result shape
| Result shape | kind |
|---|---|
| 1 time column + 1..3 metrics | line |
| 1 category + 1 metric | bar (sorted by value desc unless the order is natural: months, ranges) |
| part of a whole, fewer than 6 categories, one metric | pie |
| a single number (or latest value) | kpi |
| many categories (>12) | bar of top N plus an "Other" bucket computed in SQL |

## Rules
- Aggregate and bucket in SQL (GROUP BY the time grain / category); never rely on the UI to aggregate raw rows. Cap to roughly 500 points per line, 50 bars.
- The title states the insight or the exact metric and period, not just "Revenue by month".
- Time grain matches the question (day/week/month); truncate with the dialect's function (date_trunc / TRUNC(date,'MM')). Exclude the incomplete current period or label it.
- Order the SQL by x (time ascending, or value descending for bars).
- Alias columns with readable names; the alias is what appears on axes.
- Do not chart a metric that mixes units or currencies; split it.
- No pie for more than 5 slices; no chart at all when a table of <=3 rows says it better.

name: analysis-stats
description: Statistical analysis expressed as SQL: percentiles, moving averages, growth, outliers (z-score, IQR), cohort retention, funnel, and how to interpret pasted results. Load for trend, distribution, outlier, retention, funnel, growth or comparison questions.
body:
# Statistics in SQL (you cannot run Python; express it as a query)

## Descriptive
- Report median and p90/p95/p99, not only the mean, for skewed data (amounts, latency).
- Percentile syntax: PostgreSQL / Oracle percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY x) (Oracle: PERCENTILE_CONT(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY x)); Trino approx_percentile(x, 0.95).

## Trend
- Moving average with a window: AVG(metric) OVER (ORDER BY day ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW).
- Growth: (cur - prev) / NULLIF(prev, 0) with LAG(metric) OVER (ORDER BY period); compare equal-length periods; exclude the partial current period.
- Seasonality: compare against the same weekday / same month last year before calling something a change.

## Outliers
- z-score: ABS(x - AVG(x) OVER ()) / NULLIF(STDDEV(x) OVER (), 0) > 3. IQR: outside q1 - 1.5*iqr .. q3 + 1.5*iqr.
- Do NOT delete outliers automatically. Investigate: data error (fix/exclude and say how many rows, e.g. "excluded 47 rows, 0.3%"), genuine extreme (keep; use median/percentiles), different population (segment).

## Cohort retention, funnel (patterns)
- Cohort: cohort_month = first activity month per user (CTE), activity_month per event, months_since = difference; COUNT(DISTINCT user) / cohort size.
- Funnel: one row per user with the first timestamp of each step (MIN(CASE WHEN step=... THEN ts END)), then count users reaching each step with ordering enforced (ts_n > ts_n-1).

## Comparisons and significance
- Say sample sizes. Under ~30 events per group, call the result directional only.
- Statistical vs practical significance: give effect size and absolute difference, not just "significant". Many segments sliced = multiple comparisons: expect false positives.
- Correlation is not causation; check Simpson's paradox by splitting on the obvious confounder.

name: error-fixing
description: Turn a pasted database error (ORA-xxxxx, SQLSTATE/PostgreSQL, Trino error name) into a root cause and a corrected query. Load whenever the user pastes an error message or says a query fails.
body:
# Fixing SQL errors

Method: read the error code and position, find the exact token in the SQL, check it against the metadata block, change ONE thing, give the corrected full query, say how to confirm. After 2-3 failed attempts on the same error, stop patching: re-read the schema and the requirement.

## Oracle
| Error | Usual cause / fix |
|---|---|
| ORA-00904 invalid identifier | column does not exist, wrong alias scope (alias used in WHERE/same SELECT), quoted lowercase name; check metadata case |
| ORA-00942 table or view does not exist | wrong schema prefix, missing grant, typo |
| ORA-00979 not a GROUP BY expression | add column to GROUP BY or aggregate it |
| ORA-00933 SQL command not properly ended | LIMIT used (use FETCH FIRST n ROWS ONLY), trailing semicolon via JDBC, stray clause |
| ORA-01722 invalid number | implicit conversion of a non-numeric string; TO_NUMBER with validation, or fix the join key types |
| ORA-01843 / 01861 not a valid month / literal does not match format | use DATE 'YYYY-MM-DD' or TO_DATE(x, 'YYYY-MM-DD') |
| ORA-01427 single-row subquery returns more than one row | aggregate, add a key, or use IN/EXISTS |
| ORA-00918 column ambiguously defined | qualify with alias |
| ORA-01795 max 1000 expressions in list | use a join to a table/CTE or split the list |
| ORA-01476 divisor is equal to zero | NULLIF(denominator, 0) |

## PostgreSQL
| Error | Usual cause / fix |
|---|---|
| 42703 column does not exist | typo, mixed-case name needs double quotes, alias used in WHERE |
| 42P01 relation does not exist | schema not in search_path: schema-qualify |
| 42803 must appear in GROUP BY | add to GROUP BY or aggregate |
| 42883 operator/function does not exist | missing cast (text = integer): add ::type or fix the type |
| 22P02 invalid input syntax for type | bad literal/cast; validate input |
| 22012 division by zero | NULLIF(denominator, 0) |
| 42601 syntax error | dialect clash (TOP, FETCH vs LIMIT, backticks) |
| 21000 more than one row returned by a subquery | aggregate or LIMIT 1 with ORDER BY |
| 57014 canceling statement due to statement timeout | filter, index, narrower range (see query-performance) |

## Trino
| Error | Usual cause / fix |
|---|---|
| COLUMN_NOT_FOUND / TABLE_NOT_FOUND | name, catalog.schema.table qualification, case |
| TYPE_MISMATCH / cannot be applied to | explicit CAST; compare like with like (varchar vs bigint, date vs timestamp) |
| INVALID_FUNCTION_ARGUMENT | date_diff('day', start, end) takes the unit first; bad format string |
| EXCEEDED_LOCAL_MEMORY_LIMIT / EXCEEDED_GLOBAL_MEMORY_LIMIT | filter partitions, fewer columns, approx_distinct/approx_percentile, avoid huge ORDER BY / DISTINCT, broadcast only small sides |
| DIVISION_BY_ZERO | NULLIF(denominator, 0) |
| SYNTAX_ERROR | ILIKE is not supported (use lower(x) LIKE), backticks, TOP, trailing semicolon via JDBC |
| MISSING_GROUP_BY / not an aggregate expression | group by or aggregate the column |
| PAGE_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT / query timeout | fewer columns, LIMIT, time filter |

Always: if the error is a permission or object-not-found problem, say it may be access, not SQL, and do not rewrite the query to hide it.

name: data-context
description: Learn the business context of a connection: what entities mean, standard filters, metric formulas, gotchas; ask only the missing questions, then propose durable notes for the user to save. Load when the user says "learn", "remember this definition", explains what a table/metric/status means, corrects a query because of a business rule, or asks to onboard/document a database.
body:
# Learning business context (per connection)

Goal: make future answers on this connection correct without re-explaining. Notes are saved by the USER (you only propose them) and come back as a BUSINESS-CONTEXT block.

## 1. Take what is already known
Read the BUSINESS-CONTEXT block, the DB metadata, and (if available) OpenMetadata: descriptions, glossary terms, owners, tags. Do not ask what these already answer.

## 2. Ask only the gaps (one question at a time via ask_user, with options when possible)
- Entity meaning (most important): "customer / user / merchant / account" - which table and key, and what counts as active?
- Standard filters: what must ALWAYS be excluded (test accounts, soft-deleted rows, cancelled / reversed transactions, internal merchants)?
- Metrics: the 2-3 most requested ones, exact formula, source table, time grain, currency/unit.
- Time: which timestamp is "the date" of a transaction (created, settled, booked)? time zone? fiscal calendar?
- Gotchas: what mistakes do new analysts make here (duplicated rows, status codes, snapshots vs history)?
Stop asking when answers would not change any query.

## 3. Propose notes (propose_context_note)
- One sentence each, concrete and checkable: "Active merchant = status 'ACTIVE' and deleted_at IS NULL." / "Revenue = SUM(fee_amount) of status 'SUCCESS' transactions, VND, by settled_at."
- kind: entity | terminology | filter | metric | gotcha.
- Only facts the user stated/confirmed or that OpenMetadata states. Never a guess, never a secret or real customer value.
- At most 5 per answer; do not re-propose what is already in the context block.

## 4. Apply
When a saved note applies, use it by default and say so in one clause ("applying the standard filter: ...") so the user can correct it.

name: dialect-oracle
description: Oracle SQL specifics: row limiting, dates, NULL/empty string, string aggregation, set operators, pagination, identifiers. Load before writing Oracle SQL beyond a trivial select.
body:
# Oracle SQL

- Row limit: FETCH FIRST n ROWS ONLY (12c+); older: WHERE ROWNUM <= n applied AFTER ordering via a subquery. No LIMIT, no TOP.
- No trailing semicolon through JDBC. One statement per run.
- '' is NULL; ''  = '' is not true. Use IS NULL. NVL(a, b), NVL2(a, notnull, null), COALESCE, DECODE (prefer CASE).
- Dates: DATE has a time part; DATE 'YYYY-MM-DD' literal; TO_DATE(s, 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS'); TO_CHAR(d, 'YYYY-MM'); TRUNC(d), TRUNC(d, 'MM'), TRUNC(d, 'IW'); ADD_MONTHS(d, n); d + 1 is one day; SYSDATE / SYSTIMESTAMP; months_between; INTERVAL '7' DAY. Filter dates as half-open ranges on the raw column.
- Strings: || concatenates (NULL is treated as empty in concatenation); SUBSTR (1-based), INSTR, REGEXP_LIKE, REGEXP_SUBSTR, LISTAGG(col, ', ') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY col); no ILIKE: UPPER(a) LIKE UPPER(b).
- Types: VARCHAR2, NUMBER(p,s), no BOOLEAN column in SQL; CAST(x AS NUMBER); TO_NUMBER fails on bad input (12.2+: TO_NUMBER(x DEFAULT NULL ON CONVERSION ERROR)).
- Set operators: UNION, UNION ALL, INTERSECT, MINUS (not EXCEPT).
- Table without FROM: FROM DUAL.
- Identifiers fold to UPPER unless double-quoted; 128-byte limit from 12.2 (30 before). Do not quote identifiers unless metadata shows mixed case.
- Joins: ANSI JOIN syntax; avoid the old (+) operator.
- Analytics: ROW_NUMBER/RANK/LAG/LEAD, KEEP (DENSE_RANK FIRST ORDER BY ...) for first/last value, PERCENTILE_CONT ... WITHIN GROUP, APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT (12c+).
- Upsert: MERGE INTO t USING s ON (...) WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE ... WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT ...
- Top-N per group: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY g ORDER BY x DESC) <= n in an outer query.
- Plan: EXPLAIN PLAN FOR <sql> then SELECT * FROM TABLE(DBMS_XPLAN.DISPLAY) (two statements).

name: dialect-postgresql
description: PostgreSQL specifics: types and casts, date/time, JSONB, arrays, DISTINCT ON, FILTER, string aggregation, upsert, identifiers. Load before writing PostgreSQL SQL beyond a trivial select.
body:
# PostgreSQL SQL

- Row limit: LIMIT n [OFFSET m]; prefer keyset pagination.
- Casts: x::type or CAST(x AS type). integer / integer truncates: cast one side to numeric.
- Identifiers fold to lowercase unless double-quoted; a column created as "UserId" must be quoted every time.
- Dates: now(), current_date, date_trunc('month', ts), ts AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh', interval '7 days', ts >= date_trunc('day', now()) - interval '7 days', extract(epoch from ...), generate_series(start, stop, interval '1 day') for gap filling. timestamptz vs timestamp matters for boundaries.
- Strings: || (NULL propagates; use concat() or coalesce), ILIKE, ~ regex, split_part, string_agg(x, ', ' ORDER BY x), left/right, position.
- Conditional aggregation: COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'paid').
- First row per group: SELECT DISTINCT ON (key) ... ORDER BY key, updated_at DESC.
- JSONB: col->'a'->>'b' (text), col @> '{"k":1}', jsonb_array_elements, jsonb_each_text. Index with GIN.
- Arrays: = ANY(array), unnest, array_agg; 1-based.
- Upsert: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE SET ... ; RETURNING to see affected rows.
- Percentiles: percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY x).
- CTEs: since 12 not always materialized; use MATERIALIZED / NOT MATERIALIZED when it matters.
- Plan: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) executes the statement; only for SELECT or inside BEGIN/ROLLBACK.
- Catalog helpers: information_schema.columns, pg_indexes, pg_stat_user_tables (n_live_tup, last_analyze).

name: dialect-trino
description: Trino/Presto specifics: catalog.schema.table naming, date functions and argument order, arrays and UNNEST, approx functions, no ILIKE, partition pruning, EXPLAIN. Load before writing Trino SQL beyond a trivial select.
body:
# Trino SQL

- Names: catalog.schema.table; use the catalog shown in the metadata. Row limit: LIMIT n. No trailing semicolon via JDBC.
- No ILIKE: lower(a) LIKE lower(b). Regex: regexp_like(s, 'pat'), regexp_extract. Concat: || returns NULL if any side is NULL; use concat() / coalesce.
- Integer division truncates: CAST(a AS double) / b or a * 1.0 / b. Use try_cast and try(expr) to turn row-level errors into NULL.
- Dates: current_date, current_timestamp, now(); date_trunc('month', ts); date_add('day', 7, ts); date_diff('day', start, end) (unit first, end minus start); current_date - INTERVAL '7' DAY; from_unixtime(sec), to_unixtime(ts); format_datetime(ts, 'yyyy-MM-dd') / date_format(ts, '%Y-%m-%d'); ts AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh'; date_parse(s, '%Y-%m-%d'). Compare date columns with date literals (DATE '2025-01-15').
- Partition pruning: filter partition columns (ds, dt, year/month/day) with plain comparisons on the raw column; wrapping them in functions can disable pruning. Always bound large tables by time.
- Aggregates: approx_distinct(x), approx_percentile(x, 0.95), count_if(cond), max_by(x, y) / min_by, arbitrary(x), array_agg(x ORDER BY y), listagg(x, ', ') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY x) (newer versions) or array_join(array_agg(x), ', ').
- Arrays/maps: 1-based, a[1]; CROSS JOIN UNNEST(arr) AS t(elem); element_at(map, key) returns NULL when missing; transform, filter, cardinality.
- JSON: json_extract_scalar(col, '$.a.b'), json_parse, json_format.
- Window functions as usual; first_value/last_value need an explicit frame.
- Conditional: IF(cond, a, b), CASE, COALESCE, NULLIF.
- Introspection: SHOW CATALOGS / SCHEMAS / TABLES, SHOW COLUMNS FROM t, DESCRIBE t, SHOW CREATE TABLE t, SHOW STATS FOR t.
- EXPLAIN [ (TYPE DISTRIBUTED) ] and EXPLAIN ANALYZE (the latter executes the query).
- Large outputs: CTAS is far cheaper than returning millions of rows; but only propose CTAS if the user asked to materialize.
